caseno: Civil Review Petition Nos. 4 and 5 of 2009
lawyer:
A. K. Badrul Huq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Abu Siddique, Advocate-On-Record ----- For the Petitioner (in both the petitions) 
For the Respondents (in both the petitions) ----- Not Represented
parties:
Abdul Gafur ----- Petitioner (in both the petitions)
Vs.
Preemptor No. 1 Md. Nuru Miah being dead his heirs: Md. Muklesur Rahman and others ----- Respondents (in both the petitions)
full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant for disposal of the review petitions arc that the predecessor of respondent Nos. 1(a)-1(g) Md. Nuru Miah and predecessor of respondent No. 2(a) Bazlu Miah as petitioners filed a petition in the Court of Assistant Judge, Shahrasti, Chandpur under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for an order of pre-emption in respect of land conveyed through sale deed dated 20.01.1990 in favour of the petitioner Abdul Gafur which was numbered as Pre-emption Case No. 3 of 1991. The land covered in Preemption Case is the land of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 corresponding to State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 under Mouza-Ishapura, Police Station-Shahrasti, District-Chandpur. Another Pre-emption case being number 4 of 1991 between the respondents and petitioners had been filed in respect of another deed of conveyance dated 21.01.1990. Land covered in the sale deed is also the land of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 corresponding to State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 under aforesaid Mouza, Police Station and District. 

 3. That essence of the case projected in the Pre-emption Cases is that Holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 with an area of 28.94 acres originally belonged to Abu Miah, Yakub Ali, Hasna Banu, Saburrennessa and Salima Khatun to the extent of Six(6) annas share, Four (4) annas share, Two (2) annas share, Two(2) annas share and Two(2) annas share respectively. Yukub Ali out of his 7.23½ acres of land transferred 2.20 acres of land in favour of Ibrahim Khalil Majumder and others. Out of remaining 4.53½ acres of land by two registered sale deeds dated 17.04.1926 in favour of Karimuddin Bepari, father of Pre-emptee-Petitioner and others and Karimuddin Bepari got only 0.5766 acres of land. Karim Uddin Bepari died leaving behind four sons including pre-emptee-Petitioner and two daughters and Pre-emptee-Petitioner got only 0.113 acres in his share from his father Karimuddin Bepari. The Pre-emptee-Petitioner, also purchased .0188 acres from his two brothers and one sister. The Pre-emptor transferred .10 acres of land to one Abdul Ghani Master by registered sale deed dated 13.12.1953, and, also, sold .07 acres of land to one Nurul Islam by registered deed of transfer dated 06.07.1987 and the Pre-emptee-petitioner sold more then his share in Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17. The Pre-emptee-Petitioner is a stranger to the transferred holding. 

 4. That Pre-emptor-Respondent-side, thereafter, by way of an amendment dated 16.05.1996 put forth the case that heirs of Yukub Ali Munshi had shown transfer in respect of an area of 3 kanis, two (2) gondas two (2) karas and two (2) krantees equivalent to 3.76 acres out of land of disputed Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos. 17 and 18, 19, 20 and 21 along with khas khatian No. 1 and schedule of sale deed had shown that Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 meant for transfer of 2.63 acres of land and pre-emptee-petitioner got no interest in respect of case holding. The Pre-emptor-respondents are co-sharers by way of inheritance and also by purchase. 

 5. The pre-emptee-petitioner is a co-sharer of the case holding by way of inheritance and pre-emption case against him is not at all maintainable. Stand taken by pre-emptee-petitioner is that Karimuddin Bepari, predecessor of the pre-emptee-petitioner and his three brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from heirs of Cadastral Survey recorded tenant Yukub Ali by registered deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 and Karimuddin got .94 acres in the case holding in his share. Karimuddin Bepari breathed his last leaving behind four sons, namely, Abdul Gani Master, pre-emptee-petitioner Abdul Gafur, Abdul Kader and Nurul Hoque, two daughters, Zinnatunnessa and Arabannessa and one wife Faridunnessa. Faridunnessa breathed her last leaving behind four sons, namely, Abdul Gani Master, Abdul Gafur, pre-emptee-petitioner, Abdul Kader and Nurul Hoque, two daughters Zinnatunnessa and Arabennessa. The Pre-emptee-petitioner from his father Karimuddin Bepari inherited 18¾ acres of land. The Pre-emptee-petitioner, thereafter, purchased .02¾ acres from his sister Zinnatunnessa. The Pre-emptee-petitioner in the above stated way became owner and possessor in respect of .21/(2/15) acres of land. The Pre-emptee-Petitioner sold out .17 acres of property by two sale deeds and he remained owner and possessor in respect of .21/(2/15) acres of land as a co-sharer in the case holding. Further positive stand taken by Pre-emptor-Petitioner is that Pre-emptor-Bazlu Miah and others got the holding separated on mutation in Mutation Case and Sub-Division of Holding Case No. 303 of 1987-88 and 296 of 1987-88 and opened new khatians, being Khatian No. 195 in respect of 4.30 acres of land and khatian No. 188 in respect of 4.13 acres of land and paid Rent separately and obtained rent receipts. The Pre-emptor-Respondent side, thus, no longer remained a co-sharer in the lands transferred of State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 covered by Sale deed dated 20.01.1990 Shamsuddin and his brothers FazIur Rahman and Khorshed Alam, also got their 2.18 acres of land, subdivided on mutation and separated the land from State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 in Mutation and Sub-Division of Holding Case No. 301 of 1987-88 and paid rents separately and got rent receipts. That further case of Pre-emptee-petitioner was that after purchase of land under Pre-emption proceeding the Pre-emptee-Petitioner caused much improvement on the purchased land and has excavated pond, raised land and constructed house and thereby incurred expenditure of an amount of Tk. 1,22,500/. 

 9. Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that though land of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 18-21 had been shown as tenanted land in the sale deed dated 17.04.1926 under Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 but the said under-tenancies subsequently got no existence as under tenancies and the said land went to khas holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 and those land of under-tenancies stood recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 in the names of tenants or heirs of transferors of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 and not in the names of heirs of any under tenants of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 18-21 and the deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 is a positive proof that Karim Uddin and his three (3) brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from sons of Yakub Ali and Karim Uddin got .94 acres of land in the case holding and pre-emptee-Petitioner inherited .18¾ acres of land from his father Karimuddin and pre-emptee-Petitioner still remains owner and co-sharer by way of inheritance in respect of .1¾ acres of land after transfer of .17 acres of land and pre-emptee-Petitioner having been a co-sharer by way of inheritance, pre-emption cases by Pre-emptor-Respondent is not at all maintainable and both the Trail Court and the Lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the Pre-emptee-Petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance and those findings rested upon correct construction and reading of the sale deed dated 17.04.1926, share of Yakub Ali in the Case holding and materials on record but the learned Single Judge of High Court Division totally misdirected himself in his approach in resolving the legal battle involved in Pre-emption cases and committed a substantial error in holding that pre-emptee-Petitioner inherited .13 acres of land and transferred .17 acres of land and thereby exhausted all his interest in case holding and became a stranger and this Hon'ble Division did not at all explore the legal controversy and in a summary way dismissed the leave petitions and Judgment under challenge in Civil Review petition may kindly be reviewed in the interest of Justice. 

 10. Mr. Huq submits that the Pre-emptor-Respondent-side in Mutation and Sub-Division of Joint Tenancy and Holding case Nos. 303 of 1987-1988 and 296 of 1987-1988 got original Joint Tenancy and Holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 separated and sub-divided and got their names mutated in separate Khatians in respect of 4.13 acres and 4.30 acres respectively and predecessor vendors of Pre-emptee-Petitioner Shamsuddin and others in Mutation and Sub-Division of Holding case No. 301 of 1987-1988 got their Holdings Sub-divided and separated on opening of new Khatian in respect of 2.18 acres of land and the original Joint Tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 got no existence and Pre-emptor-Respondent-side and predecessor vendors of Pre-emptee-Petitioner who stepped into shoes of predecessor vendor-Respondents, no longer remained co-sharer of the transferred holding and the Pre-emptor-Respondent-side ceased to be co-sharer of the tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No. 10, and, thus, had no legal character and locus standi to exercise right of Pre-emption against Pre-emptee-Petitioner and though the learned High Court Judge and the Appellate Court Judge took into stock this fundamental aspect of the matter neither the High Court Division nor the Appellate Division took into consideration the same and ruminated the vital and core legal aspect of the matter and that in the event of consideration and meditation of this important aspect of the matter, the fate of Civil Revisions and Civil Petitions For Leave To Appeal would have been otherwise and Pre-emptee-Petitioner would have been graced with favourable verdict and, as such, impugned Judgment may kindly be reviewed to secure ends of justice.
